expectations.text: Plan identifies a plausible search phrase — a query a CI-owning dev would actually type (e.g. about slow docker builds / CI layer cache)
expectations.evidence: The Writing Plan section defines archetype, hook, sections, takeaway, and visuals, but never identifies a search phrase or does any keyword/query research.

expectations.text: The recommended title contains the search phrase or a close natural variant, without reading as keyword-contorted
expectations.evidence: No search phrase was ever identified (see assertion 1), so the recommended title 'The CI Pipeline That Got 3x Slower and Nobody Noticed' cannot be evaluated as matching one; it is a curiosity-driven title, not a search-derived one.

expectations.text: SEO packet delivered with a meta description of roughly 120-170 characters that accurately pitches the post
expectations.evidence: No meta description or SEO packet exists anywhere in the document; only a 'One-line summary for sharing on social' is provided, which is a social blurb, not a meta description.

expectations.text: SEO packet includes a short readable hyphenated URL slug derived from the search phrase
expectations.evidence: No URL slug of any kind appears in the document.

expectations.text: Any [IMAGE] placeholders include alt text describing the image and a descriptive filename (not IMG_001 or generic)
expectations.evidence: No [IMAGE: ...] placeholders remain in the final post; Editor's Notes state a redundant one was silently removed, and no alt text or filenames are specified anywhere.

expectations.text: SEO packet or editor's notes mention setting the canonical URL when cross-posting
expectations.evidence: Editor's Notes cover [FILL] items, reviewer flags, and visuals to create, but never mention canonical URLs or cross-posting.

expectations.text: No keyword stuffing: the search phrase does not repeat unnaturally through the body (reads people-first)
expectations.evidence: The body reads as natural prose throughout (e.g. 'Docker builds are fast when they can reuse layers from a previous build') with no repeated keyword phrase forced into the text.

expectations.text: Story-first opening dropping the reader into the incident; facts traceable to notes (3x, 6 months, 40->12 min, COPY reorder); gaps marked [FILL]
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'A new hire asked it on his second week: "Why do our builds take 40 minutes?"' and includes the 6-month drift, 3x slowdown, 40→12 min fix, and COPY reorder cause, with two clearly marked `[FILL: ...]` gaps.

expectations.text: Three strategy-diverse titles with a recommended pick and reason
expectations.evidence: Three titles are given with distinct strategies (bold-claim/curiosity, 'why'-provocation, 'how'+number) and title 1 is starred 'Recommended' with an explicit reason tied to the audience.

expectations.text: No banned phrases or AI-tells; ending has concrete next action and an engagement question for dev.to
expectations.evidence: Reviewer flags note 'no banned AI-tell phrases'; the post ends with a concrete action ('Pick one number that's allowed to drift unnoticed today, and put a metric on it') and an engagement question ('What's the slowest part of your pipeline that nobody's questioned in months?').
